numerical_failure.affected_api: jax._src.lax.lax.tanh_p (default tanh JVP rule for lax.tanh)
numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Default `tanh` JVP rule computed derivatives using `(g + g * ans) * (1 - ans)`, which could break bit-for-bit even symmetry when `g != 1`, so `jvp(-x) == jvp(x)` and `grad(-x) == grad(x)` may fail.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Default `tanh` JVP rule should compute derivatives using `g * ((1 + ans) * (1 - ans))`, which evaluates `(1 + ans) * (1 - ans)` before scaling by `g` to avoid premature rounding when `g != 1` and guarantees bit-for-bit even symmetry (`jvp(-x) == jvp(x)` and `grad(-x) == grad(x)`).
trigger_conditions: Using the default `tanh` JVP rule with a scaling factor `g` such that `g != 1`.
Checking symmetric-input derivative consistency at `x` and `-x`, i.e. verifying `jax.jvp(lax.tanh, (x,), (g,))` equals `jax.jvp(lax.tanh, (-x,), (g,))`.
Checking gradient symmetry via `jax.grad` at `x` and `-x` (bit-for-bit equality).

oracle_clues: The fix explicitly targets symmetry of the default `tanh` JVP rule: it must guarantee bit-for-bit even symmetry `jvp(-x) == jvp(x)` and `grad(-x) == grad(x)`.
The discrepancy is attributed to premature rounding when `g != 1` in the old expression `(g + g * ans) * (1 - ans)`.
The added test `LaxTest.testTanhGradSymmetry` asserts bit-for-bit equality using `self.assertArraysEqual` for both forward-mode (`jax.jvp`) and reverse-mode (`jax.grad` via `jax.vmap`).

category_specific_evidence: The fix is for “symmetry of default tanh JVP rule” and changes the expression from `(g + g * ans) * (1 - ans)` to `g * ((1 + ans) * (1 - ans))` to avoid premature rounding when `g != 1` and to guarantee “bit-for-bit even symmetry (`jvp(-x) == jvp(x)` and `grad(-x) == grad(x)`)”.

`LaxTest.testTanhGradSymmetry` verifies forward- and reverse-mode derivative symmetry by setting `x = jnp.linspace(0.1, 8.9, 100, dtype=jnp.float32)` and `g = jnp.full_like(x, 1.3)`, then computing `jax.jvp(lax.tanh, (x,), (g,))` and `jax.jvp(lax.tanh, (-x,), (g,))` and asserting `self.assertArraysEqual(jvp_pos, jvp_neg)`.
The same test verifies symmetry of gradients using `grad_fn = jax.vmap(jax.grad(lambda z: jnp.float32(1.3) * lax.tanh(z)))` and checks `self.assertArraysEqual(grad_fn(x), grad_fn(-x))`.
The PR body states the reasoning: evaluating `(1 + ans) * (1 - ans)` before scaling by `g` “avoids premature rounding when `g != 1`” and “guarantees bit-for-bit even symmetry”.
An additional metadata test changes an XLA metadata type for `('tanh(x)', jnp.tanh, ...)` from `add` to `multiply`, but does not state dtype/precision/magnitude/tolerance.

No evidence specifies a numeric tolerance threshold separating correct vs incorrect answers; tests use `assertArraysEqual` (bit-for-bit) rather than an `atol/rtol` tolerance.
No evidence specifies a broader magnitude regime beyond the tested range `x in [0.1, 8.9]`; behavior outside this range may differ.
No evidence specifies precision mode (e.g., `AccuracyMode`), though the `_exp2_lower(..., accuracy)` snippet is unrelated to `tanh` symmetry.

provenance.value: The default `tanh` JVP rule used the expression `(g + g * ans) * (1 - ans)`, which could break bit-for-bit even symmetry of derivatives when `g != 1` (i.e., fails to guarantee `jvp(-x) == jvp(x)` and `grad(-x) == grad(x)` due to premature rounding).

Use the expression `g * ((1 + ans) * (1 - ans))` so that evaluating `(1 + ans) * (1 - ans)` before scaling by `g` avoids premature rounding when `g != 1` and guarantees bit-for-bit even symmetry (`jvp(-x) == jvp(x)` and `grad(-x) == grad(x)`).
